# Roy Gardner

## Overview

- **Age:** Early twenties  <sub>[v3 c25 P29](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0029), [v3 c25 P38](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0038)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v3 c25 P28](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0028)</sub>
- **Status:** Single  <sub>[v3 c38 P21](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0021)</sub>
- **Origin:** Kingsport, Nova Scotia  <sub>[v3 c4 P62](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0062), [v3 c24 P1](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0001)</sub>
- **Role:** College student  <sub>[v3 c25 P38](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0038)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Roy  <sub>[v3 c25 P29](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0029)</sub>

## Appearance

Roy is a tall, remarkably handsome young man with a slender, distinguished build, dark hair, and melacholy, inscrutable, dark velvety eyes. He possesses a memorable, deep, and meltingly sympathetic voice, an expressive smile, and an impeccably stylish manner of dress.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P28](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0028), [v3 c25 P29](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0029), [v3 c25 P35](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0035), [v3 c25 P44](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0044), [v3 c28 P24](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0024), [v3 c35 P14](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0014)_

## Personality

Roy is an intensely romantic, gallant, and poetically inclined young man who delights in expressing his feelings through elegant compliments, sonnets, and grand gestures. He is unfailingly courteous, gentle, and refined, maintaining a polished and serious demeanor. Although sincere in his passions, he lacks a strong sense of humor and tends to be somewhat uninteresting or lacking in depth beneath his ideal, hero-like exterior. When experiencing disappointment, he becomes deeply earnest, dramatic, and sorrowful, though he eventually recovers from his romantic heartbreaks.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P28](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0028), [v3 c25 P44](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0044), [v3 c25 P48](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0048), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v3 c38 P17](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0017), [v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027), [v3 c38 P32](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0032), [v3 c39 P2](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0002)_

## History

Roy Gardner completed his Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond College before taking a two-year hiatus to accompany his ailing mother to Europe. Upon returning to Kingsport to resume his Junior year, he met Anne Shirley in the park during a sudden autumn rainstorm and offered her the shelter of his umbrella. Infatuated by her beauty and intellect, he began ardently courting her, sending her flowers, poetry, and lavish attentions over the next two years. His family eventually accepted the relationship and hosted Anne, cementing his place as her recognized suitor throughout their time at Redmond. Near the end of their Senior year, Roy took Anne to the harbor pavilion where they first shared an umbrella and formally proposed marriage to her. When Anne unexpectedly rejected him, realizing she did not truly love him, Roy was heartbroken, bitterly accused her of ruining his life, and departed. After their parting, he slowly recovered from his grief, leaving Anne to return home to Avonlea.

## Background by volume

- Member of a very wealthy and prominent Kingsport family  <sub>[v3 c24 P1](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0001), [v3 c25 P46](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0046)</sub>
- His father passed away prior to his college years  <sub>[v3 c25 P46](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0046)</sub>

## Quotes

> Pardon me—may I offer you the shelter of my umbrella?  <sub>[v3 c25 P28](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0028)</sub>

> I feel as if I didn’t belong anywhere yet. I put in my Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond two years ago. I’ve been in Europe ever since. Now I’ve come back to finish my Arts course.  <sub>[v3 c25 P38](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0038)</sub>

> You have ruined my life.  <sub>[v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027)</sub>

> I can’t understand it—I can’t believe you are not the woman I’ve believed you to be. But reproaches are idle between us. You are the only woman I can ever love. I thank you for your friendship, at least. Good-bye, Anne.  <sub>[v3 c38 P32](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0032)</sub>
